description: Agroforestry is a land-use system that deliberately combines trees with crops and/or animals on the same piece of land to gain ecological and economic benefits.

mcq.questionText: What is the meaning of agroforestry?

options.text: Growing only forest trees for timber production
Deliberately combining trees with crops and/or animals on the same land
Keeping animals in a fenced area without any trees
Growing crops in a greenhouse without soil

mcq.explanation: Agroforestry is a land-use system where trees are grown together with crops and/or livestock on the same piece of land for combined benefits.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a basic component of agroforestry?
mcq.explanation: The three main components of agroforestry are trees, crops and animals; machinery such as tractors is not a component of the system.

mcq.questionText: The form of agroforestry that combines trees with crops only is called:
mcq.explanation: Agrisilviculture is the practice of growing trees together with crops on the same land.

mcq.questionText: Which form of agroforestry combines trees with pasture and animals?
mcq.explanation: Silvopasture is the agroforestry system in which trees are grown together with pasture for grazing animals.

mcq.questionText: Agrosilvopasture is best described as a system that combines:
mcq.explanation: Agrosilvopasture integrates all three components of agroforestry: trees, crops and animals on the same piece of land.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a benefit of agroforestry?

options.text: It provides fuel wood, fodder and shade
It removes all nutrients from the soil

mcq.explanation: Agroforestry provides many benefits including fuel wood, fodder for animals and shade, while also conserving the soil.

mcq.questionText: How do tree roots in an agroforestry system help in soil conservation?

options.text: They loosen the soil so it is washed away easily
They bind the soil particles and reduce erosion
They make the soil acidic and bare
They prevent water from entering the soil

mcq.explanation: Tree roots hold soil particles firmly together, reducing the effect of running water and wind, thereby controlling soil erosion.

mcq.questionText: Which tree species is commonly used in agroforestry because it fixes nitrogen and provides fodder?
mcq.explanation: Leucaena is a leguminous agroforestry tree that fixes nitrogen in the soil and provides nutritious fodder for livestock.

mcq.questionText: Leguminous agroforestry trees improve soil fertility mainly by:

options.text: Adding nitrogen to the soil through their root nodules
Drinking all the water in the soil
Blocking sunlight completely from the soil

mcq.explanation: Leguminous trees have root nodules containing bacteria that fix atmospheric nitrogen, enriching the soil with this nutrient.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best explains how agroforestry contributes to environmental conservation?

options.text: By increasing carbon dioxide in the air
By absorbing carbon dioxide and reducing global warming
By drying up all rivers and streams

mcq.explanation: Trees in agroforestry absorb carbon dioxide during photosynthesis, helping to reduce greenhouse gases and combat global warming.

mcq.questionText: Fallen tree leaves in an agroforestry system are useful because they:

options.text: Decompose to form humus that improves soil fertility
Stop rain from reaching the ground

mcq.explanation: Decomposed tree leaves form humus that adds organic matter and nutrients to the soil, improving its fertility and structure.

mcq.questionText: Which benefit of agroforestry directly helps a farmer earn money?

options.text: Sale of timber, fruits and fuel wood from trees
Increase in weeds on the farm

mcq.explanation: Agroforestry provides income because farmers can sell products such as timber, fruits, poles and fuel wood from the trees.

mcq.questionText: A good agroforestry tree should have which of the following characteristics?

options.text: Deep roots that do not compete much with crops
Very wide spreading shallow roots that compete with crops
A poisonous nature that kills nearby crops
Very slow growth and no useful products

mcq.explanation: A suitable agroforestry tree should have deep roots so it does not compete strongly with crops for water and nutrients near the surface.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of planting trees along the boundaries of a farm in agroforestry?

options.text: They act as a windbreak and provide poles
They increase soil erosion by wind
They reduce the value of the land

mcq.explanation: Boundary trees serve as windbreaks that protect crops from strong winds and also supply poles, fuel wood and other products.

mcq.questionText: Why might too many large trees in a crop field reduce crop yield in agroforestry?

options.text: They add too much nitrogen to crops
Their heavy shade and roots compete with crops for light, water and nutrients
They make crops grow faster than normal
They have no effect on crops at all

mcq.explanation: When trees are too many or too large, their dense shade and roots compete with crops for sunlight, water and nutrients, lowering yields.

fib.explanation: Agroforestry deliberately integrates trees with crops and/or livestock for combined ecological and economic benefits.

fib.questionText: The three main components of agroforestry are trees, crops and _____.
fib.explanation: Trees, crops and animals are the three basic components combined in agroforestry systems.

fib.questionText: The form of agroforestry that combines trees with crops only is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Agrisilviculture is the growing of trees together with crops on the same piece of land.

fib.questionText: The form of agroforestry that combines trees with pasture and grazing animals is called _____.
fib.explanation: Silvopasture integrates trees with pasture and livestock on the same land.

fib.questionText: The agroforestry system that combines trees, crops and animals all together is called _____.
fib.explanation: Agrosilvopasture uses all three components: trees, crops and animals on the same land.

fib.questionText: Trees that have root nodules and add nitrogen to the soil are called _____ trees.
fib.explanation: Leguminous trees fix atmospheric nitrogen through bacteria in their root nodules, improving soil fertility.

fib.questionText: Wood from agroforestry trees that is used for cooking and heating is called _____ wood.
fib.explanation: Fuel wood (firewood) is one of the important products obtained from agroforestry trees.

fib.questionText: The leaves and branches of agroforestry trees fed to livestock are called _____.
fib.explanation: Fodder is plant material, including tree leaves, used to feed farm animals.

fib.questionText: Tree roots help in soil conservation by holding soil particles together and reducing _____.
fib.explanation: By binding soil particles, tree roots reduce the washing away of soil by water and wind.

fib.questionText: Trees in agroforestry help reduce global warming by absorbing the gas called _____.
fib.explanation: During photosynthesis, trees take in carbon dioxide, reducing the amount of this greenhouse gas in the air.

tf.questionText: Agroforestry means growing trees together with crops and/or animals on the same piece of land.
tf.explanation: This is the correct definition of agroforestry as a combined land-use system.

tf.questionText: Trees, crops and animals are the three main components of agroforestry.
tf.explanation: Agroforestry combines trees with crops and/or animals, which are its three basic components.

tf.questionText: Silvopasture is the agroforestry system that combines trees with crops only.
tf.explanation: Silvopasture combines trees with pasture and animals; the system combining trees with crops only is agrisilviculture.

tf.questionText: Agrosilvopasture combines trees, crops and animals on the same piece of land.
tf.explanation: Agrosilvopasture integrates all three agroforestry components together.

tf.questionText: Agroforestry increases soil erosion on the farm.
tf.explanation: Agroforestry reduces soil erosion because tree roots bind the soil and tree cover protects it from rain and wind.

tf.questionText: Leguminous agroforestry trees improve soil fertility by adding nitrogen to the soil.
tf.explanation: Leguminous trees fix atmospheric nitrogen through their root nodules, enriching the soil.

tf.questionText: Fuel wood, fodder and shade are some of the benefits obtained from agroforestry.
tf.explanation: Agroforestry trees provide fuel wood, fodder for animals and shade, among other benefits.

tf.questionText: A good agroforestry tree should have shallow, spreading roots that strongly compete with crops.
tf.explanation: A good agroforestry tree should have deep roots so it competes less with crops for water and nutrients near the surface.

tf.questionText: Agroforestry trees help in environmental conservation by absorbing carbon dioxide from the air.
tf.explanation: Trees absorb carbon dioxide during photosynthesis, helping to reduce greenhouse gases and global warming.

tf.questionText: Planting too many large trees in a crop field always increases crop yield.
tf.explanation: Too many large trees create heavy shade and root competition for light, water and nutrients, which can reduce crop yield.

hoq.questionText: A farmer in a dry area wants to plant trees among his maize crop to improve soil fertility without greatly reducing maize yield. Which choice is most suitable?

options.text: A fast-growing leguminous tree with deep roots planted at wide spacing
Many large shallow-rooted trees planted very close to the maize
Trees that produce dense shade over the whole field
Trees that take up large amounts of water from the topsoil

hoq.explanation: A deep-rooted leguminous tree at wide spacing fixes nitrogen to improve fertility while minimising competition with maize for light, water and surface nutrients.

hoq.questionText: A hillside farm is losing fertile topsoil during the rainy season. How can agroforestry best be used to solve this problem?

options.text: Removing all trees so water flows faster down the slope
Planting rows of trees along the contour to slow runoff and hold the soil
Ploughing up and down the slope between bare ground
Leaving the land bare during the rains

hoq.explanation: Planting trees along the contour slows down running water and their roots bind the soil, greatly reducing soil erosion on the slope.

hoq.questionText: Why is agrosilvopasture often considered more sustainable than growing a single crop alone on the same land over many years?

options.text: It relies on only one source of income and one product
It combines trees, crops and animals so resources are used efficiently and risks are spread
It quickly exhausts soil nutrients and increases erosion
It removes all organic matter from the soil each season

hoq.explanation: Agrosilvopasture diversifies products and income, recycles nutrients between trees, crops and animals, and protects the soil, making the system more sustainable than monoculture.
